study_identification.title: Mapping the Heterogeneous Phenotype of Schizophrenia and Bipolar Disorder Using Normative Models

study_characteristics.study_objective: Quantify brain-structural heterogeneity in schizophrenia and bipolar disorder by mapping individual deviations from a normative model, and assess how group-level analyses may mask inter-individual abnormalities.

The threshold for individual deviation maps was established at |z|>2.6 ... we also performed the analyses again controlling the FDR ...

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Group comparisons of mean deviations and percent of extreme deviating voxels using PALM and χ2 tests; regressions relating percent extreme deviations to age, disease duration, and cognition with Bonferroni-Holm correction; additional regressions to assess relationships with image quality, medication load, and substance abuse.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Individual deviations from the normative model were frequent but highly heterogeneous in both schizophrenia and bipolar disorder; overlap >2% occurred only in few loci, with schizophrenia showing mean gray matter reductions in frontal, temporal, and cerebellar regions and bipolar disorder primarily in cerebellum.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Using GPR-based normative models, patients exhibited significantly more extreme deviations than controls, yet voxelwise overlap across patients exceeded 2% only in limited regions. Schizophrenia showed mean negative deviations in frontal, temporal, and cerebellar gray matter, while bipolar disorder showed mean deviations predominantly in cerebellar regions. Associations indicated that, in schizophrenia, extreme positive white matter deviations related to longer disease duration, and in bipolar disorder, greater extreme negative gray matter deviations related to lower processing speed and executive function (eTable 2). Conclusions replicated under FDR-based thresholding of extremes (supplement).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Cross-sectional design limits causal inference; specific confound handling (e.g., medication, substance abuse, motion) is exploratory and limited; only general image quality metric used; single-site acquisition may limit generalizability.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Demonstrates normative modeling for individual-level mapping; suggests moving beyond case–control averages; proposes future stratification via clustering of deviation patterns and multimodal integration; supplementary FreeSurfer analyses support VBM findings.

general_notes.general_notes: Single 1.5T scanner (Siemens Sonata). Primary analysis at voxel level (VBM via CAT12/SPM12) with 8 mm smoothing; supplementary vertex-level FreeSurfer (v5.3) analyses of cortical thickness and surface area. All analyses conducted in Python 3.6; PALM used for permutation inference on deviation maps.
